svg.title: CHISUM: Stern ramp and after end, JS3-304 revision 0
svg.text: Stern ramp and after end: arrangement, hydraulics, lights · JS3-304 · revision 0 · 11 November 2026

Johansson Shipyard, newbuilding No. 1, rebuilt at 68 m for Johansson Line. Drawn from the numbers her model is built from. A working drawing of what is built; no force, weight or rule is calculated here.
Metres. Heights over the design waterline.
A THE TRANSOM, SEEN FROM ASTERN
Port to the left. What stands on the upper deck forward of the stern is left out.
The stern to the left. The ramp raised, level, and at its lowest (dashed); the cylinder raised and level.
C PLAN AT THE CAR DECK, THE RAMP LOWERED
Port up. The lights stand above, on the bulwark and the transom; the ramp raised is dashed.
Two double-acting cylinders, one each side of the roadway: they push the ramp down and pull it up. Each is 1.90 m of
barrel from its foot pin; its rod runs out 1.29 m in all. With slopes kept within 10° the ramp's end meets a quay
between 1.07 and 2.55 m over the water. Tide, trim and the quays she will use are not studied.
THE LIGHTS OF THE AFTER END
white, unbroken over 135° astern: 67.5° each side of right aft; a screen forward of it
on the centreline, its glass 7.72 m over the waterline and 0.11 m abaft the transom, on the
component NLT-06 of the register: navigation light panel, circuit 4
white, looking aft and 50° down: the middle of each beam meets the quay 5.2 m abaft the
on posts on the bulwark's rail, 3.60 m each side of the centreline, 8.00 m over the

on the transom 3.60 m to starboard of the centreline, its foot 2.45 m over the car deck:
beside the door, on the driver's side
not yet in the register: no circuit
The opening in the transom over the car deck, 6.40 m wide and 4.30
m clear: two of her four lanes at a time.
One leaf, 6.36 m wide and 4.27 m from the hinge to its end, drawn
0.10 m deep. Raised, it is the stern door. It lowers 100°: level
at 90°, and 10° further for a quay that lies lower. Its roadway
has bars across it against slipping.
On the sill of the door, 0.01 m over the car deck and 0.09 m
inside the transom; a lug at each end of the sill stays when the
Double-acting, 3.02 m each side of the centreline, inside the
opening's width. Foot pin on the pedestal, rod pin on a lug on the
ramp 0.90 m from the hinge. 3.04 m between the pins raised, 4.26 m
level. The roadway between the two is 5.86 m.
A column on a footplate on the car deck, 3.20 m inside the
transom, stayed forward and aft; the foot pin 1.60 m over the
deck. In line with the door's jambs, so the lanes are clear of it.
White, over 135° astern. See the table of the lights.
For the ramp and the quay at night. See the table.
For those who drive aboard. See the table.
On stocks 2.40 m from the transom, 2.40 m each side of the
centreline; the tillers in the steering gear room under the car
2.00 m, 3.80 m from the transom, on shafts that rise 8° forward
and enter her about 9.1 m from the transom.
Not hers and not given: drawn level with the car deck, the ramp
The hydraulic power unit, its pipes and the stand the ramp is worked
from are not drawn or placed.
No force is calculated: the ramp's weight, the cylinders' bore and
pressure, the pins and the pedestals' seating on the deck's
How the raised ramp is held and made tight against the sea (cleats,
a seal) is not drawn: a stern door of a passenger ship has to be
The ramp has no lip or flaps to the quay, and its own structure is
not designed: it is drawn as a slab.
The floodlights and the signal have no place in the component
register yet, so no cable, circuit or switch.
The sternlight's arc is drawn as the rule asks; it is not yet
measured in the model as the bridge's lanterns are (JS4-404).
The quays she will lie at, their heights and the tide are not known:
the 10° either way is an assumption.
The owner, 11 November 2026: "Does it need to be wider?" Not for
what she carries: 6.40 m serves two of her four lanes at a time,
with 5.86 m between the cylinders: cars two abreast, lorries one at
a time. Two lorries abreast would ask about 7.4 m (the yard's
estimate, from no rule). Not decided.
All three views at this scale.
